samples.claim: UpdateBases iterates proposals after candidate construction/range conversion. Reject if any existing BasePath has equal Option name OR equal path; two absent names therefore conflict too. For id0 allocate current maximum ID+1 or1 with ordinary arithmetic. Nonzero supplied ID is inserted without separate collision check, so it can overwrite a different same-ID entry if name/path checks pass. New proposals see previously inserted proposals; no mutation to current manifest, no URI reachability/path normalization check here.
samples.review_note: Exact name-OR-path conflict, absent-name equality, max+1 allocation and unchecked supplied-ID insertion match; preceding apply_range_segments confirms ordering.

samples.claim: Public ConditionalPutCommitHandler has definitive NotFound=true and propagate-after-success=false. It creates a fresh memory store, calls the injected writer at dummy, ignores its WriteResult, then reads all dummy bytes and derives actual size. Manifest mutations precede durable publication, and complete serialized bytes remain in memory. A callback that does not create dummy fails at readback.
samples.review_note: Both policy hooks, fresh memory store, dummy callback and ignored WriteResult/full read match. Supplemental read_one_all opens the path then gets all bytes; actual publication follows this range.

Slice comments explicitly identify Box<[T]> and Arc<[T]> as owners that count slice bytes; adding those bytes again in the slice implementation would double-count them.

samples.claim: Private decode_content revalidates version, then scans complete content. Legacy tag1 decodes protobuf Version and lifts each group, in received order, into one OrderedCompaction transition using old/new digests and unchanged bitmap bytes. Legacy dataset_version is ignored; graph ordering later replaces version ordering. Every lifted transition passes decode_transition, so malformed legacy data can fail stricter ledger checks. The original serialized Any is not retained in returned ledger.
samples.review_note: Version validation, legacy group lifting and preserved bitmap bytes match. Supplemental loop tail orders lineage and constructs graph maps without retaining original Any.

samples.claim: Private merge_fragments_valid docs say one-to-one preservation/only add columns or rows, but implementation first rejects only a smaller proposed vector length. It permits extra fragments. Then builds HashMap<u64,&Fragment>, retaining last proposed occurrence of each ID. No ID uniqueness/sort check; extra duplicates can satisfy count check while map hides earlier entries. O(proposed count) expected map construction and reference storage.
samples.review_note: Only a smaller proposed fragment count is rejected here; HashMap collection uses last duplicate ID, matching the narrower implementation than one-to-one documentation.

samples.claim: sorted_sequence_sizes returns [holes,bitmap,array] estimates using u128:24+4*n_holes,24+ceil(total_slots/8),24+2*count, each saturating and then converting to usize with MAX fallback. Assumed four-byte holes and two-byte array entries need not match selected EncodedU64Array width/base or actual protobuf tags/lengths. Return order matters for ties. This function expects valid sorted stats.
samples.review_note: All three u128 cost formulas and return order match; supplemental helper confirms usize MAX fallback. Estimates differ from concrete widths and are not exact wire measurements.

samples.claim: Synchronous approximations return entry_count as usize and weighted_size_bytes without maintenance; comments explicitly warn weighted_size can be stale. These report declared/rounded eviction accounting, not shared-buffer-aware deep allocation totals.
